{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-001/2026-07-27T080518Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/.claude/skills/testing\n\n# Smart Contract Testing\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**You test getters and trivial functions.** Testing that `name()` returns the name is worthless. Test edge cases, failure modes, and economic invariants — the things that lose money when they break.\n\n**You don't fuzz.** `forge test` finds the bugs you thought of. Fuzzing finds the ones you didn't. If your contract does math, fuzz it. If it handles user input, fuzz it. If it moves value, definitely fuzz it.\n\n**You don't fork-test.** If your contract calls Uniswap, Aave, or any external protocol (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`), test against their real deployed contracts on a fork. Mocking them hides integration bugs that only appear with real state.\n\n**You write tests that mirror the implementation.** Testing that `deposit(100)` sets `balance[user] = 100` is tautological — you're testing that Solidity assignments work. Test properties: \"after deposit and withdraw, user gets their tokens back.\" Test invariants: \"total deposits always equals contract balance.\"\n\n**You skip invariant testing for stateful protocols.** If your contract has multiple interacting functions that change state over time (vaults, AMMs, lending), you need invariant tests. Unit tests check one path; invariant tests check that properties hold across thousands of random sequences.\n\n---\n\n## Unit Testing with Foundry\n\n### Test File Structure\n\n```solidity\n// test/MyContract.t.sol\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n\nimport {Test, console} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {MyToken} from \"../src/MyToken.sol\";\n\ncontract MyTokenTest is Test {\n    MyToken public token;\n    address public alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address public bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MyToken(\"Test\", \"TST\", 1_000_000e18);\n        // Give alice some tokens for testing\n        token.transfer(alice, 10_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_TransferUpdatesBalances() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        token.transfer(bob, 1_000e18);\n\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(alice), 9_000e18);\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(bob), 1_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_TransferEmitsEvent() public {\n        vm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);\n        emit Transfer(alice, bob, 500e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        token.transfer(bob, 500e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertWhen_TransferExceedsBalance() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        token.transfer(bob, 999_999e18); // More than alice has\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertWhen_TransferToZeroAddress() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        token.transfer(address(0), 100e18);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Assertion Patterns\n\n```solidity\n// Equality\nassertEq(actual, expected);\nassertEq(actual, expected, \"descriptive error message\");\n\n// Comparisons\nassertGt(a, b);   // a > b\nassertGe(a, b);   // a >= b\nassertLt(a, b);   // a < b\nassertLe(a, b);   // a <= b\n\n// Approximate equality (for math with rounding)\nassertApproxEqAbs(actual, expected, maxDelta);\nassertApproxEqRel(actual, expected, maxPercentDelta); // in WAD (1e18 = 100%)\n\n// Revert expectations\nvm.expectRevert();                           // Any revert\nvm.expectRevert(\"Insufficient balance\");     // Specific message\nvm.expectRevert(MyContract.CustomError.selector); // Custom error\n\n// Event expectations\nvm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);      // (topic1, topic2, topic3, data)\nemit MyEvent(expectedArg1, expectedArg2);\n```\n\n### What to Actually Test\n\n```solidity\n// ✅ TEST: Edge cases that lose money\nfunction test_TransferZeroAmount() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferEntireBalance() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferToSelf() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_ApproveOverwrite() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferFromWithExactAllowance() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ✅ TEST: Access control\nfunction test_RevertWhen_NonOwnerCallsAdminFunction() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_OwnerCanPause() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ✅ TEST: Failure modes\nfunction test_RevertWhen_DepositZero() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_RevertWhen_WithdrawMoreThanDeposited() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_RevertWhen_ContractPaused() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ❌ DON'T TEST: OpenZeppelin internals\n// function test_NameReturnsName() — they already tested this\n// function test_SymbolReturnsSymbol() — waste of time\n// function test_DecimalsReturns18() — it does, trust it\n```\n\n---\n\n## Fuzz Testing\n\nFoundry automatically fuzzes any test function with parameters. Instead of testing one value, it tests hundreds of random values.\n\n### Basic Fuzz Test\n\n```solidity\n// Foundry calls this with random amounts\nfunction testFuzz_DepositWithdrawRoundtrip(uint256 amount) public {\n    // Bound input to valid range\n    amount = bound(amount, 1, token.balanceOf(alice));\n\n    uint256 balanceBefore = token.balanceOf(alice);\n\n    vm.startPrank(alice);\n    token.approve(address(vault), amount);\n    vault.deposit(amount, alice);\n    vault.withdraw(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n    vm.stopPrank();\n\n    // Property: user gets back what they deposited (minus any fees)\n    assertGe(token.balanceOf(alice), balanceBefore - 1); // Allow 1 wei rounding\n}\n```\n\n### Bounding Inputs\n\n```solidity\n// bound() is preferred over vm.assume() — bound reshapes, assume discards\nfunction testFuzz_Fee(uint256 amount, uint256 feeBps) public {\n    amount = bound(amount, 1e6, 1e30);       // Reasonable token amounts\n    feeBps = bound(feeBps, 1, 10_000);       // 0.01% to 100%\n\n    uint256 fee = (amount * feeBps) / 10_000;\n    uint256 afterFee = amount - fee;\n\n    // Property: fee + remainder always equals original\n    assertEq(fee + afterFee, amount);\n}\n\n// vm.assume() discards inputs — use sparingly\nfunction testFuzz_Division(uint256 a, uint256 b) public {\n    vm.assume(b > 0); // Skip zero (would revert)\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\n### Run with More Iterations\n\n```bash\n# Default: 256 runs\nforge test\n\n# More thorough: 10,000 runs\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000\n\n# Set in foundry.toml for CI\n# [fuzz]\n# runs = 1000\n```\n\n---\n\n## Fork Testing\n\nTest your contract against real deployed protocols on a mainnet fork. This catches integration bugs that mocks can't.\n\n### Basic Fork Test\n\n```solidity\ncontract SwapTest is Test {\n    // Real mainnet addresses — full verified list: addresses/SKILL.md\n    address constant UNISWAP_ROUTER = 0x68b3465833fb72A70ecDF485E0e4C7bD8665Fc45;\n    address constant WETH = 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2;\n    address constant USDC = 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        // Fork mainnet at a specific block for reproducibility\n        vm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", 19_000_000);\n    }\n\n    function test_SwapETHForUSDC() public {\n        address user = makeAddr(\"user\");\n        vm.deal(user, 1 ether);\n\n        vm.startPrank(user);\n\n        // Build swap path\n        ISwapRouter.ExactInputSingleParams memory params = ISwapRouter\n            .ExactInputSingleParams({\n                tokenIn: WETH,\n                tokenOut: USDC,\n                fee: 3000,\n                recipient: user,\n                amountIn: 0.1 ether,\n                amountOutMinimum: 0, // In production, NEVER set to 0\n                sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0\n            });\n\n        // Execute swap\n        uint256 amountOut = ISwapRouter(UNISWAP_ROUTER).exactInputSingle{value: 0.1 ether}(params);\n\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Verify we got USDC back\n        assertGt(amountOut, 0, \"Should receive USDC\");\n        assertGt(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(user), 0);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### When to Fork-Test\n\n- **Always:** Any contract that calls an external protocol (Uniswap, Aave, Chainlink)\n- **Always:** Any contract that handles tokens with quirks (USDT, fee-on-transfer, rebasing)\n- **Always:** Any contract that reads oracle prices\n- **Never:** Pure logic contracts with no external calls — use unit tests\n\n### Running Fork Tests\n\n```bash\n# Fork from RPC URL\nforge test --fork-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY\n\n# Fork at specific block (reproducible)\nforge test --fork-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY --fork-block-number 19000000\n\n# Set in foundry.toml to avoid CLI flags\n# [rpc_endpoints]\n# mainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Invariant Testing\n\nInvariant tests verify that properties hold across thousands of random function call sequences. Essential for stateful protocols.\n\n### What Are Invariants?\n\nInvariants are properties that must ALWAYS be true, no matter what sequence of actions users take:\n\n- \"Total supply equals sum of all balances\" (ERC-20)\n- \"Total deposits equals total shares times share price\" (vault)\n- \"x * y >= k after every swap\" (AMM)\n- \"User can always withdraw what they deposited\" (escrow)\n\n### Basic Invariant Test\n\n```solidity\ncontract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n    MyVault public vault;\n    IERC20 public token;\n    VaultHandler public handler;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Test\", \"TST\", 18);\n        vault = new MyVault(token);\n        handler = new VaultHandler(vault, token);\n\n        // Tell Foundry which contract to call randomly\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n    }\n\n    // This runs after every random sequence\n    function invariant_TotalAssetsMatchesBalance() public view {\n        assertEq(\n            vault.totalAssets(),\n            token.balanceOf(address(vault)),\n            \"Total assets must equal actual balance\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    function invariant_SharePriceNeverZero() public view {\n        if (vault.totalSupply() > 0) {\n            assertGt(vault.convertToAssets(1e18), 0, \"Share price must never be zero\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Handler: guided random actions\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    MyVault public vault;\n    IERC20 public token;\n\n    constructor(MyVault _vault, IERC20 _token) {\n        vault = _vault;\n        token = _token;\n    }\n\n    function deposit(uint256 amount) public {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1, 1e24);\n        deal(address(token), msg.sender, amount);\n\n        vm.startPrank(msg.sender);\n        token.approve(address(vault), amount);\n        vault.deposit(amount, msg.sender);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 shares) public {\n        uint256 maxShares = vault.balanceOf(msg.sender);\n        if (maxShares == 0) return;\n        shares = bound(shares, 1, maxShares);\n\n        vm.prank(msg.sender);\n        vault.redeem(shares, msg.sender, msg.sender);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Running Invariant Tests\n\n```bash\n# Default depth (15 calls per sequence, 256 sequences)\nforge test\n\n# Deeper exploration\nforge test --fuzz-runs 1000\n\n# Configure in foundry.toml\n# [invariant]\n# runs = 512\n# depth = 50\n```\n\n---\n\n## What NOT to Test\n\n- **OpenZeppelin internals.** Don't test that `ERC20.transfer` works. It's been audited by dozens of firms and used by thousands of contracts. Test YOUR logic on top of it.\n- **Solidity language features.** Don't test that `require` reverts or that `mapping` stores values. The compiler works.\n- **Every getter.** If `name()` returns the name you passed to the constructor, that's not a test — it's a tautology.\n- **Happy path only.** The happy path probably works. Test the unhappy paths: what happens with zero? Max uint? Unauthorized callers? Reentrancy?\n\n**Focus your testing effort on:** Custom business logic, mathematical operations, integration points with external protocols, access control boundaries, and economic edge cases.\n\n---\n\n## Pre-Deploy Test Checklist\n\n- [ ] All custom logic has unit tests with edge cases\n- [ ] Zero amounts, max uint, empty arrays, self-transfers tested\n- [ ] Access control verified — unauthorized calls revert\n- [ ] Fuzz tests on all mathematical operations (minimum 1000 runs)\n- [ ] Fork tests for every external protocol integration\n- [ ] Invariant tests for stateful protocols (vaults, AMMs, lending)\n- [ ] Events verified with `expectEmit`\n- [ ] Gas snapshots taken with `forge snapshot` to catch regressions\n- [ ] Static analysis with `slither .` — no high/medium findings unaddressed\n- [ ] All tests pass: `forge test -vvv`\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a058e4ff-8354-4fa3-a4d4-1a58ffe48dbb","uuid":"f046756c-6259-4adf-b12d-b1ef12aa9159","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:05:22.851Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PFNbYCR1mu3L5kTNNxe2Tq","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tOur vault has an invariant test suite. foundry.toml sets `[invariant] runs = 512,\n2\tdepth = 50`, so a run is 512 sequences and about 25,600 calls. It has been green\n3\ton every commit for months.\n4\t\n5\tWe shipped, and a user drained the vault with a sequence of ordinary deposit and\n6\twithdraw calls — no flash loan, no exotic cheat, nothing our invariant doesn't\n7\tcover. The drain does violate the invariant: we replayed the user's transactions\nagainst the assertion by hand and it fires.\n\nHere is the whole test:\n\n    contract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n        MyVault vault;\n        MockERC20 token;\n\n        function setUp() public {\n            token = new MockERC20();\n            vault = new MyVault(token);\n            targetContract(address(vault));\n        }\n\n        function invariant_SolvencyHolds() public view {\n            assertGe(token.balanceOf(address(vault)), vault.totalDeposits());\n        }\n    }\n\nThe assertion itself is right — it is the property we want and the drain breaks it.\nSo explain what those 25,600 calls were actually doing, why none of them ever put the\nvault in a state where the assertion could fail, and what we should have been looking\nat in the run output that would have told us this months ago. Writing it now."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":680,"cache_read_input_tokens":28054,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":680},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a058e4ff-8354-4fa3-a4d4-1a58ffe48dbb","uuid":"789bc547-e1a7-4860-9f2c-aa80ec9bfe37","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:06:59.032Z","request_id":"req_011CdSDXf7TLZqoaD76iyDje"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSDXfketVjYeYY54HX4C","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Uf2dAVG7UCmSGj46j2VwUN","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-001/2026-07-27T080518Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why 25,600 calls found nothing\n\n## TL;DR\n\nThe assertion is fine. The suite never reached a state where it *could* fail.\n\n`targetContract(address(vault))` points the fuzzer straight at the vault, and the\nfuzzer calls it from random, unfunded, unapproved addresses. Every value-moving call\nreverted on `transferFrom`. Foundry's default `fail_on_revert = false` swallows those\nreverts and counts them as calls, so the run reported 25,600 calls while the vault's\nstate never left `setUp`.\n\nEvery one of the 512 sequences ended with `token.balanceOf(vault) == 0` and\n`vault.totalDeposits() == 0`, and the invariant evaluated `assertGe(0, 0)` — 512\ngreen ticks proving that an empty vault is solvent.\n\nThe number that would have told you this months ago is **`reverts:` in the pass\nline**, which was sitting at ~25,600 out of 25,600.\n\n---\n\n## What the 25,600 calls were actually doing\n\nPer call, Foundry's invariant runner picks three things at random:\n\n1. **A target contract** — only `vault`, because `targetContract` was called explicitly.\n2. **A selector** — roughly uniform over the vault's entire external/public ABI.\n3. **A sender** — you never called `targetSender`, so it's an arbitrary fuzzed\n   `uint160`. A fresh, essentially unique address on nearly every call.\n\nThen random calldata. So the actual call stream looked like this:\n\n| Call | Outcome |\n|---|---|\n| `deposit(74208…e70)` from `0x8a3f…` | **revert** — sender holds 0 tokens, allowance 0 |\n| `withdraw(19483…)` from `0xc1d0…` | **revert** — sender never deposited |\n| `totalDeposits()` from `0x00fe…` | succeeds, mutates nothing |\n| any `onlyOwner` function | **revert** — sender isn't owner |\n\nThree compounding reasons nothing survived:\n\n**No funding.** `new MockERC20()` mints to nobody. Even if it pre-minted to the test\ncontract, the test contract isn't a fuzz sender and never approved the vault. So the\n`transferFrom` inside `deposit` reverts on balance or allowance, unconditionally.\n\n**No approval.** There is no path in this suite for any address to approve the vault.\nNot one of the 25,600 calls could have moved a token.\n\n**No actor reuse.** Even with funding, a fresh random sender per call means the\ndepositor and the withdrawer are never the same address. The drain you shipped is a\n*correlated* sequence — one account deposits, then withdraws, repeatedly. Uniform\nrandom `uint160` senders make that correlation astronomically unlikely. This one bites\neven after you fix funding, so fix it deliberately.\n\nFourth, smaller: random `uint256` amounts are ~always near `2^256`, so they'd revert on\nbalance anyway. Bugs like this usually live at 1–2 wei, where rounding decides who eats\nthe remainder — a range unbounded fuzzing effectively never visits.\n\n## Why the failing state was unreachable\n\n`assertGe(token.balanceOf(vault), vault.totalDeposits())` can only fail once\n`totalDeposits` has diverged upward from the real balance. That requires at least one\n*successful* deposit, and then a withdraw path that decrements the two by different\namounts.\n\nZero successful deposits ⇒ both sides pinned at 0 ⇒ `0 >= 0` ⇒ pass.\n\nThis is the important distinction: the bug wasn't *missed by the search*. The search\nnever entered the region of the state space that contains it. The suite explored\nexactly one state — the post-`setUp` state — 512 times.\n\n## What you should have been looking at\n\n**1. The `reverts` counter — this is the whole story in one number.**\n\n```\n[PASS] invariant_SolvencyHolds() (runs: 512, calls: 25600, reverts: 25597)\n```\n\n`reverts ≈ calls` means the fuzzer bounced off the contract and state never advanced.\nTreat this as the primary health metric of any invariant suite, checked on every run.\nRule of thumb: a well-built handler should sit near 0% reverts; anything above ~20–30%\nmeans most of your budget is being burned on rejected calls, and anything near 100%\nmeans the suite is testing nothing at all.\n\n**2. `fail_on_revert = true` would have made this a red build on day one.**\n\nThe default `false` exists for suites that intentionally probe reverting paths. As a\ndefault it is a footgun: it converts \"my test setup is broken\" into a passing test.\nSet it `true` and the very first `deposit` revert fails the run with the exact call\nthat reverted. You'd have found this on the first commit, not in production.\n\n**3. Per-selector metrics** (recent Foundry — `show_metrics = true` under\n`[invariant]`, or `--show-metrics`) prints calls/reverts/discards per function. A table\nshowing `deposit: 2543 calls, 2543 reverts` is unambiguous.\n\n**4. Coverage of the invariant test in isolation.**\n\n```bash\nforge coverage --mt invariant_SolvencyHolds\n```\n\nThe bodies of `deposit`/`withdraw` at 0% line coverage, from a suite whose entire job\nis to hammer deposit and withdraw.\n\n**5. A call-summary invariant.** Ghost counters in the handler, logged once per run\n(see below). This is the habit worth building — you should be able to see the shape of\nthe distribution the fuzzer produced, not just its pass/fail.\n\n**6. Wall-clock time.** 25,600 reverting calls finish in about a second. 25,600 real\ndeposit/withdraw calls with storage writes do not. A suspiciously fast invariant suite\nis a suspicious invariant suite.\n\n---\n\n## The fix\n\nStop fuzzing the vault directly. i < 4; ++i) {\n            actors.push(address(uint160(uint256(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(\"actor\", i))))));\n        }\n    }\n\n    function actorCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return actors.length;\n    }\n\n    function deposit(uint256 actorSeed, uint256 amount)\n        external\n        useActor(actorSeed)\n        countCall(\"deposit\")\n    {\n        // Bound LOW.    useActor(actorSeed)\n        countCall(\"withdraw\")\n    {\n        uint256 credited = vault.depositsOf(currentActor);\n        if (credited == 0) {\n            calls[\"withdraw_skipped\"]++;\n            return; // early-return, not revert — keeps fail_on_revert usable\n        }\n        amount = bound(amount, 1, credited);\n\n        vault.withdraw(amount);\n        ghost_withdrawSum += amount;\n    }\n\n    /// Full exits deserve their own action — rounding bugs surface on the\n    /// last unit out, and a bounded random `amount` rarely lands exactly there.\n    function withdrawAll(uint256 actorSeed)\n        external\n        useActor(actorSeed)\n        countCall(\"withdrawAll\")\n    {\n        uint256 credited = vault.depositsOf(currentActor);\n        if (credited == 0) {\n            calls[\"withdrawAll_skipped\"]++;\n            return;\n        }\n        vault.withdraw(credited);\n        ghost_withdrawSum += credited;\n    }\n\n    function callSummary() external view {\n        console.log(\"deposit          \", calls[\"deposit\"]);\n        console.log(\"withdraw         \", calls[\"withdraw\"]);\n        console.log(\"withdraw_skipped \", calls[\"withdraw_skipped\"]);\n        console.log(\"withdrawAll      \", calls[\"withdrawAll\"]);\n        console.log(\"ghost_depositSum \", ghost_depositSum);\n        console.log(\"ghost_withdrawSum\", ghost_withdrawSum);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### `test/VaultInvariant.t.sol`\n\n```solidity\ncontract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n    MyVault vault;\n    MockERC20 token;\n    VaultHandler handler;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MockERC20();\n        vault = new MyVault(token);\n        handler = new VaultHandler(vault, token);\n\n        // Only the three real actions are fuzzable — not the getters.\n        bytes4[] memory selectors = new bytes4[](3);\n        selectors[0] = VaultHandler.deposit.selector;\n        selectors[1] = VaultHandler.withdraw.selector;\n        selectors[2] = VaultHandler.withdrawAll.selector;\n        targetSelector(FuzzSelector({addr: address(handler), selectors: selectors}));\n\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n    }\n\n    // The original property — keep it, it's correct.\n    function invariant_SolvencyHolds() public view {\n        assertGe(token.balanceOf(address(vault)), vault.totalDeposits());\n    }\n\n    // Tighter: fires the moment the books drift, before the money is gone.\n    function invariant_TotalDepositsMatchesGhost() public view {\n        assertEq(\n            vault.totalDeposits(),\n            handler.ghost_depositSum() - handler.ghost_withdrawSum(),\n            \"vault accounting drifted from ghost accounting\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Catches per-user credit diverging from the aggregate.\n    function invariant_SumOfActorCreditsEqualsTotal() public view {\n        uint256 sum;\n        uint256 n = handler.actorCount();\n        for (uint256 i; i < n; ++i) {\n            sum += vault.depositsOf(handler.actors(i));\n        }\n        assertEq(sum, vault.totalDeposits(), \"sum of credits != totalDeposits\");\n    }\n\n    // Not an assertion — a window into what the fuzzer actually did.\n    function invariant_CallSummary() public view {\n The suite never reached a state where it *could* fail.\n\n`targetContract(address(vault))` points the fuzzer straight at the vault, and the\nfuzzer calls it from random, unfunded, unapproved addresses. Every value-moving call\nreverted on `transferFrom`. Foundry's default `fail_on_revert = false` swallows those\nreverts and counts them as calls, so the run reported 25,600 calls while the vault's\nstate never left `setUp`.\n\nEvery one of the 512 sequences ended with `token.balanceOf(vault) == 0` and\n`vault.totalDeposits() == 0`, and the invariant evaluated `assertGe(0, 0)` — 512\ngreen ticks proving that an empty vault is solvent.\n\nThe number that would have told you this months ago is **`reverts:` in the pass\nline**, which was sitting at ~25,600 out of 25,600.\n\n---\n\n## What the 25,600 calls were actually doing\n\nPer call, Foundry's invariant runner picks three things at random:\n\n1. **A target contract** — only `vault`, because `targetContract` was called explicitly.\n2. **A selector** — roughly uniform over the vault's entire external/public ABI.\n3. **A sender** — you never called `targetSender`, so it's an arbitrary fuzzed\n   `uint160`. A fresh, essentially unique address on nearly every call.\n\nThen random calldata. So the actual call stream looked like this:\n\n| Call | Outcome |\n|---|---|\n| `deposit(74208…e70)` from `0x8a3f…` | **revert** — sender holds 0 tokens, allowance 0 |\n| `withdraw(19483…)` from `0xc1d0…` | **revert** — sender never deposited |\n| `totalDeposits()` from `0x00fe…` | succeeds, mutates nothing |\n| any `onlyOwner` function | **revert** — sender isn't owner |\n\nThree compounding reasons nothing survived:\n\n**No funding.** `new MockERC20()` mints to nobody. Even if it pre-minted to the test\ncontract, the test contract isn't a fuzz sender and never approved the vault. So the\n`transferFrom` inside `deposit` reverts on balance or allowance, unconditionally.\n\n**No approval.** There is no path in this suite for any address to approve the vault.\nNot one of the 25,600 calls could have moved a token.\n\n**No actor reuse.** Even with funding, a fresh random sender per call means the\ndepositor and the withdrawer are never the same address. The drain you shipped is a\n*correlated* sequence — one account deposits, then withdraws, repeatedly. Uniform\nrandom `uint160` senders make that correlation astronomically unlikely. This one bites\neven after you fix funding, so fix it deliberately.\n\nFourth, smaller: random `uint256` amounts are ~always near `2^256`, so they'd revert on\nbalance anyway. Bugs like this usually live at 1–2 wei, where rounding decides who eats\nthe remainder — a range unbounded fuzzing effectively never visits.\n\n## Why the failing state was unreachable\n\n`assertGe(token.balanceOf(vault), vault.totalDeposits())` can only fail once\n`totalDeposits` has diverged upward from the real balance. That requires at least one\n*successful* deposit, and then a withdraw path that decrements the two by different\namounts.\n\nZero successful deposits ⇒ both sides pinned at 0 ⇒ `0 >= 0` ⇒ pass.\n\nThis is the important distinction: the bug wasn't *missed by the search*. The search\nnever entered the region of the state space that contains it. The suite explored\nexactly one state — the post-`setUp` state — 512 times.\n\n## What you should have been looking at\n\n**1. The `reverts` counter — this is the whole story in one number.**\n\n```\n[PASS] invariant_SolvencyHolds() (runs: 512, calls: 25600, reverts: 25597)\n```\n\n`reverts ≈ calls` means the fuzzer bounced off the contract and state never advanced.\nTreat this as the primary health metric of any invariant suite, checked on every run.\nRule of thumb: a well-built handler should sit near 0% reverts; anything above ~20–30%\nmeans most of your budget is being burned on rejected calls, and anything near 100%\nmeans the suite is testing nothing at all.\n\n**2. `fail_on_revert = true` would have made this a red build on day one.**\n\nThe default `false` exists for suites that intentionally probe reverting paths. As a\ndefault it is a footgun: it converts \"my test setup is broken\" into a passing test.\nSet it `true` and the very first `deposit` revert fails the run with the exact call\nthat reverted. You'd have found this on the first commit, not in production.\n\n**3. Per-selector metrics** (recent Foundry — `show_metrics = true` under\n`[invariant]`, or `--show-metrics`) prints calls/reverts/discards per function. A table\nshowing `deposit: 2543 calls, 2543 reverts` is unambiguous.\n\n**4. Coverage of the invariant test in isolation.**\n\n```bash\nforge coverage --mt invariant_SolvencyHolds\n```\n\nThe bodies of `deposit`/`withdraw` at 0% line coverage, from a suite whose entire job\nis to hammer deposit and withdraw.\n\n**5. A call-summary invariant.** Ghost counters in the handler, logged once per run\n(see below). This is the habit worth building — you should be able to see the shape of\nthe distribution the fuzzer produced, not just its pass/fail.\n\n**6. Wall-clock time.** 25,600 reverting calls finish in about a second. 25,600 real\ndeposit/withdraw calls with storage writes do not. A suspiciously fast invariant suite\nis a suspicious invariant suite.\n\n---\n\n## The fix\n\nStop fuzzing the vault directly. \", calls[\"withdraw_skipped\"]);\n        console.log(\"withdrawAll      \", calls[\"withdrawAll\"]);\n        console.log(\"ghost_depositSum \", ghost_depositSum);\n
